ai.description: The Nicobar frog reaches 4–5 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and prominent, interrupted longitudinal skin ridges.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya nicobariensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged, light-colored vertebral stripe running from the snout to the vent.
ai.habitat: The Nicobar frog inhabits tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests, often found near streams, marshes, or paddy fields at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nicobar frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp forest floor and near freshwater streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya nicobariensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season, laying clutches of small, pigmented eggs in shallow, stagnant water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya nicobariensis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands of India, where it inhabits low-elevation tropical forests and coastal areas.
ai.callDescription: The Nicobar Frog produces a series of short, rhythmic, high-pitched "chirp" notes, typically heard from flooded grasslands and marshy habitats.
